description: Enable a client-side encryption key pair (users.settings.cse.keypairs.enable). An enabled key pair can encrypt, decrypt and sign again. Needs the gmail.settings.basic scope. Workspace only: a consumer account is refused naming its tier. Runs as a background job: returns a job_id at once and the result arrives as a follow-up message. Optional account (email or alias) picks the connected Google account; the result names the account used. Parameters: account, key_pair_id. Optional API query parameters on this verb: fields (partial response), pretty_print (JSON formatting), quota_user (quota attribution, at most 40 characters), xgafv (Google $.xgafv error format: 1 or 2), alt (json only; proto/media are rejected before a request because settings results are typed JSON).
embedding_description: Turn a disabled Gmail client-side encryption key pair back on, so a Workspace user can again encrypt, decrypt and sign mail with it, for example after it was disabled by mistake or a suspected compromise was cleared.

result_processor_customizations.action_label: Gmail: Enable CSE Key Pair queued
result_processor_customizations.result_description: Job queued; completion is delivered automatically and names the account used.
result_processor_customizations.output_action_guidance: Return exactly one action using the active IO plugin's post_message (process_key: plugin::<io_plugin>::post_message). Use the provided session_id. Keep the message short and friendly. Do NOT invent process identifiers (no present_result, no status actions).

error_processor_customizations.action_context: Dispatch a background Gmail job: Gmail: Enable CSE Key Pair.
error_processor_customizations.error_interpretation: gsuite.not_connected: no Google account linked. gsuite.unknown_account: the account argument names no connected account (the message lists them). gsuite.workspace_only: the verb is a Google Workspace feature and the account is a consumer Gmail account (the message names the tier). gsuite.invalid_params: a parameter broke a rule (the message names it) or Google rejected the request (400). gsuite.missing_scope: the account's grant lacks the scope this call needs (the message names gmail.settings.basic and the reconnect step, or gmail.settings.sharing and the service-account requirement). gsuite.auth_expired: Google rejected the token (Testing-mode OAuth apps expire refresh tokens after 7 days). gsuite.not_found: the id or address does not exist in this account. gsuite.rate_limited: Gmail quota hit. gsuite.permission_denied: Google refused for another reason.
error_processor_customizations.recovery_guidance: Follow the message: reconnect with connect_account for auth_expired or missing_scope on gmail.settings.basic, use a Workspace account for workspace_only, ask a Workspace administrator for a domain-wide-delegation service account for gmail.settings.sharing, pick a listed account for unknown_account, fix the named parameter for invalid_params, retry later for rate_limited.
